analysis:
Examined the head text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 1-996) and the changed ranges. The visible change is in the media-through-CBv2 path (lines ~789-823). It computes `reasoningPrefix` from the rendered media prompt tokens via ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix, falling back to contentSeed, and passes `stopStringScope: ReasoningStopScope.scope(...)` into bridge.submitTokenized. The same prefix is reused by makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream (lines ~846-850), replacing what was apparently computed later in the base. The old stream-construction lines are removed beyond the visible head range (changed ranges at 1043-1044 and 1426-1428 are not in the supplied text).

Security-relevant observations:
- No new data egress, no crypto change, no cache-scope change. Cache scope (`requestCacheScope`), `cacheEnabled` and `hybridPrefixIdentity` plumbing are unchanged, so T-041 mitigations (authenticated cacheSalt, HMAC lookup) are not affected.
- The tokenizer decode of the prompt tail happens locally on the already-decrypted prompt. It is not logged, and reasoningPrefix is a think-tag marker string, not prompt content.
- Reservation and release paths (mediaGate.release, releaseBox.fire) are unchanged. The new code sits after mediaGate.release and inside the do/catch that releases on error, so no leaked reservation or lease was introduced. The decode closure cannot throw.
- stopStringScope is a parser-state/stop-string behavior (output correctness, not an authorization or confidentiality boundary). Whether the engine/bridge correctly handles the new `stopStringScope` parameter in submitTokenized is outside the supplied evidence (EngineV2Bridge and ReasoningStopScope were not supplied).

Remaining questions for integration: confirm that the submitTokenized signature and ReasoningStopScope exist and that the removed lines 1043-1044/1426-1428 changes are consistent. These are correctness/compile concerns, not security regressions. No findings.
